title: Pareto-Improving Pricing: Why 3 Is Better Than 2
abstract: arXiv:2609.22652v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the design of priority pricing systems with heterogeneous agents in environments in which improving quality for some agents reduces the average quality that can be provided. Contrary to the equity-efficiency tradeoff emphasized in public debates, we show that under economically natural conditions priority pricing can Pareto-improve on an equal-allocation benchmark. Three priority tiers suffice for such an improvement, combining higher quality for a fee, lower quality with compensation, and an intermediate tier at the benchmark quality; two tiers are never enough. Our results provide a framework for overcoming equity-efficiency tensions in applications such as lane pricing, waiting-line design, public provision, and insurance.

translated_title: 帕累托改进定价：为什么3比2更好
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在异质性主体环境下优先级定价系统的设计问题，这类环境的特点是提高某些主体的服务质量会降低整体可提供的平均质量。与公共辩论中常强调的公平-效率权衡相反，我们证明了在经济上自然的条件下，优先级定价可以相对于均等分配基准实现帕累托改进。三个优先级层级足以实现这种改进，即结合付费获得更高质量、接受补偿接受较低质量、以及处于基准质量的中间层级这三个选项；而两个层级永远不够。我们的结果为在车道收费、排队系统设计、公共服务供给和保险等应用中化解公平与效率之间的矛盾提供了一个框架。
tldr: 该论文证明在经济自然条件下，仅需三个优先级层级的定价系统（付费获得更高质量、接受补偿获得较低质量、以及基准质量的中间层级）即可在均等分配基准上实现帕累托改进，而两个层级永远不够，从而化解了公平与效率之间的固有矛盾。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that under economically natural conditions, a three-tier priority pricing system—combining higher quality for a fee, lower quality with compensation, and an intermediate benchmark-quality tier—suffices to Pareto-improve on an equal-allocation benchmark, while two tiers are never enough, thus overcoming the equity-efficiency tradeoff.
